claims.text: A machine-learning-based potential can improve the representation of atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation by the machine-learning potential will increase overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
The proposed intervention is development of a machine-learning-based potential.
The method is applicable from equiatomic to non-equiatomic compositions.
The method is applicable at temperatures near and above the alloys' melting temperatures.
Atomic configurations and local chemical orderings are the structural mediators affected by the intervention.
Relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references, the machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–50%.
TOR-TILD's EAM references provide the comparison baseline.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys within specified composition and temperature ranges.
The exact mismatch reduction and transferability across different high-entropy alloys remain uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning potential reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by less than 10% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
